root_cause.text: The ALSA ctxfi `atc_get_resources()` DAIO initialization loop was refactored to enumerate all `DAIOTYP` values, but it incorrectly included `SPDIF1` for hw20k2 even though that type has no corresponding definition there, leading to invalid DAIO lookup and a kernel crash.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says the refactoring “now it loops over all enum DAIOTYP entries” and that “the last entry, SPDIF1, is a special type ... and there is no corresponding definition for hw20k2,” which “caused a kernel crash on hw20k2”; the patch fixes this by adding `i == SPDIFI1` to the skip condition in `atc_get_resources()` and only mapping `SPDIFIO` to `SPDIFI1` for `CTSB073X`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE says the refactoring “now it loops over all enum DAIOTYP entries” and that “the last entry, SPDIF1, is a special type ... and there is no corresponding definition for hw20k2,” which “caused a kernel crash on hw20k2”; the patch fixes this by adding `i == SPDIFI1` to the skip condition in `atc_get_resources()` and only mapping `SPDIFIO` to `SPDIFI1` for `CTSB073X`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip the SPDIFI1 resource entry and preserve the CTSB073X SPDIFIO-to-SPDIFI1 mapping when acquiring DAIO resources.
intent_record.what: In atc_get_resources(), the loop condition was expanded to also skip i == SPDIFI1, and the assignment to da_desc.type was rewritten from a ternary expression into an explicit if/else that maps only CTSB073X with i == SPDIFIO to SPDIFI1, otherwise using i directly.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code no longer requests a DAIO resource for SPDIFI1 as a loop iteration target, while still allowing the CTSB073X SPDIFIO case to be represented internally as SPDIFI1 when fetching the resource. This avoids treating SPDIFI1 as a separately enumerated resource and preserves the special model-specific mapping only where needed.

grouping_result.intent: Skip the SPDIFI1 resource entry and preserve the CTSB073X SPDIFIO-to-SPDIFI1 mapping when acquiring DAIO resources.

relevance_review.reason: The change explicitly skips the SPDIFI1 resource entry during DAIO resource acquisition, which directly matches the root cause of incorrectly including SPDIF1 in the hw20k2 DAIO enumeration and causing an invalid lookup/crash.

candidates.rationale: This loop was refactored to enumerate all DAIOTYP values, which is the direct place where an unsupported type such as SPDIF1 could be included for hw20k2 and later passed into DAIO lookup, triggering the crash.

This assignment controls which DAIO type is requested. In the vulnerable path, it blindly uses the enumerated index for non-CTSB073X models, allowing an invalid type like SPDIF1 to be requested on hw20k2.
This is the failing lookup call that receives the invalid DAIO description. The crash occurs when the earlier loop/assignment feeds an unsupported type into this resource acquisition.

vuln_statements.explanation: This assignment selects the DAIO type for each loop iteration. In the vulnerable code, non-CTSB073X models use the raw enumerated index, which can include SPDIF1 even though hw20k2 has no corresponding definition, causing an invalid DAIO lookup.
This loop was widened to enumerate all DAIOTYP values, which allowed the unsupported SPDIF1 type to be considered for hw20k2 and then passed down into DAIO acquisition, triggering the crash.
This is the resource lookup that receives the invalid DAIO description produced by the loop and type assignment. It is the failing operation that crashes when SPDIF1 is requested on hw20k2.
